title: Review of lab1 membrane_evo c1 (SIBDH, L7[L3]): selection replicates on 3 fresh seeds against the identical-event twin, but it is carried by imposed disk deaths and the [L3] bracket rests on a contour channel; Weak
summary: I looked at the claim's pack (membrane_evo_up seed 4) and re-ran the up arm and its identical-event twin (membrane_evo) with labkit on new seeds 21 and 22 (rerun/, twin/), and ran the thread's own ledger evotrack.py for both arms on seeds 21, 22, 23 (ledger/). Final K2 biomass share up vs twin: 0.93 vs 0.46, 0.78 vs 0.30, 0.82 vs 0.02 (3/3 seeds up > twin); K2 cell counts 8/5/10 vs 5/5/1. Deaths are dominated by the imposed r=14 disks and fall on K1 (disk deaths K1 23/33/31 vs K2 1/0/2 in up), so the disk-refuge, disturbance-mediated character the claim records replicates too. Hygiene: conversions 0 in up seeds 21 and 22 but 1 each way in seed 23, which also has 1 first acquisition; off-kind daughters 0/3/2 in up vs 0/0/0 in the twin. Reproduction from noise replicates (labkit max generation 3 and 4, persistent splits 11 and 7, merge/split 0.24 and 0.09).

observations.D: rerun/seed21/lineage.png: max generation 3, 11 persistent splits, merge/split 0.24; seed 22: generation 4, 7 persistent splits, 0.09
observations.H: ledger/up_s2{1,2,3}.json vs ledger/twin_s2{1,2,3}.json: final K2 biomass share 0.93/0.78/0.82 vs 0.46/0.30/0.02; K2 births 10/4/18 vs 7/9/2; K1 disk deaths 23/33/31 vs K2 1/0/2

seeds_run.result: pass on share (0.82 vs 0.02) with hygiene lapses: 1 first acquisition, 1 conversion each way, 2 off-kind daughters

controls_run.H: twin/ and ledger/twin_s2*.json: identical-event twin (b2=b) on the same seeds

verdicts.limitation: Selection runs through imposed disk deaths (an external disturbance acting as a size refuge for K2), not intrinsic deaths; K2 cells are few and large. B is not credited here: the claimed wall channel is 4phi(1-phi), an algebraic contour (capped Weak by rubric v2), and the independent link channel L reaches rim/core 1.47 in my rerun (rerun/seed21/radial.png), just under 1.5. No resolution or dt test. Births are counted by evotrack's overlap census, which is not merge-aware.
